title: The five-minute sit spot: do nothing, notice everything
description: Naturalists have a practice called a sit spot: return to the same outdoor place, sit still, and simply notice. Five quiet minutes in a forest or garden will show you more than an hour of walking past it all.
author: SparkKindly · AI-assisted

body.heading: Choose your spot
paragraphs: Pick one place you can reach easily and often: a bench on a woodland path, a garden chair, a flat rock, the base of one particular tree. It must be ordinary enough to visit weekly — the whole method depends on returning to the same spot as the seasons change it.

Sit down, set a gentle timer for five minutes, and put your phone away. For the first minute, just listen: count how many different sounds you can separate. Birds, wind, water, distant traffic, your own breathing.

body.heading: Notice in layers
paragraphs: Next, look close: the nearest square metre of ground. Ants on errands, a spider's anchor line, seeds, fungi, the exact green of new leaves. Then look far: the shape of the canopy, the weather arriving, the light moving.

When your five minutes end, note three things you noticed in a small notebook — date, place, three lines. That notebook becomes the real treasure: after a dozen visits it reads like a diary of a place that was never empty, only unwatched.

takeaway: Same spot, five minutes, phone away: listen first, then look close, then look far — and write down three things you noticed.
materials: A place to sit outdoors: a bench, cushion or mat
A gentle timer (a phone on silent, put away after setting, works)
supervision: No supervision is needed for adults; children should be accompanied by an adult who takes a sit spot nearby.
safetyNotes: Choose a spot away from traffic, steep drops and water edges, and stay on paths where the land asks you to.
Dress for sitting still — you cool down faster than when walking — and check for ticks after sitting in long grass in tick season.
If the weather turns or you feel unsafe at any point, end the sit and leave; the spot will wait for you.
